result: Finite-group normalized/clipped GRPO expectation can be integrated by multinomial REWARD-count cases, with fixed old policy and a fixed trajectory reward table. This is not raw expected reward gradient.

definitions.trajectory: t with old joint probability p0(t), current per-slot ratio rho_s(t)

assumptions: All p0, rewards, advantages and B coefficients stopped during surrogate differentiation
Independent ancestral trajectory draws with replacement, as in the tested group estimator
Finite enumerated complete trajectories; per-slot clipping and slot summation specified
Reward is a function of one terminal program on its fixed feedback episode, not of the other sampled programs
Separate exact joint KL can be added; it was not part of this synthetic check

prospective_bound.example: 4 tokens at each of2slots ->16 complete programs, G8
prospective_bound.note: Combinatorial count only, not a timing/native/efficacy result. Early visual action encodings and full exact reward tables remain unbudgeted. No general compute-efficiency claim.

relation_to_prior_work.boundary: Simulated multi-phase few-shot tasks already exist (LIMIT); no novelty claim for creating such episodes.
Conditional prompt generation already exists (CoCoOp); adding a conditioning network is not a distinct contribution.
Meta-prompt initialization and gradient regulation are prior work (GRAM); do not relabel them GRPO.

decision: Exact same-surrogate control is algebraically feasible for a small finite program, but the representation construction action, deployable state, transferable TRAIN feedback, gradient paths, novelty and full compute budget are not yet concrete. NOT PROMOTED; no new FIRST, native, scientific fit or old endpoint scan. R89 remains closed.
